the impact of economic restructuring on the Australian labour movement, and the implications of this restructuring for the future of the labour movement and labour relations in Australia.

globalisation and the pressures for change that it has generated are not in themselves the cause of the problems of the Australian economy.
the Australian economy is in a very difficult situation.

global restructuring is a complex process, which cannot be reduced to any single dimension or factor; it is a process which involves a variety of factors, which are themselves subject to different interpretations and which are themselves interrelated in different ways in different countries.

we have been able to identify some of the dimensions of global restructuring that have been brought to bear on Australia.

the idea of decentralising labour relations is not a panacea.
